problem: A particle $P$ of mass $3\,kg$ moves along the $x$-axis from rest at the origin with an acceleration of magnitude $\frac{1}{2}{t}^{2}\,{m/s}^{2},$ where the acceleration acts in the direction of increasing $x,$ and $t\ge 0$ is the time in seconds. Calculate the change in kinetic energy of the particle between the times $t=1\,s$ and $t=2\,s.$
worked_solution:
The change in kinetic energy of a particle with mass $m,$ initial velocity ${v}_{0},$ and final velocity ${v}_{1}$ is given by

$$
Δ\,\text{KE}=\frac{1}{2}m{v}_{1}^{2}-\frac{1}{2}m{v}_{0}^{2}.
$$

When the mass and velocity are measured in kilograms and meters per second, respectively, the particle's kinetic energy is measured in Joules ($J$).

First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\ v(t) & =\int \frac{1}{2}{t}^{2}\,\text{d}t \\ v(t) & =\frac{1}{6}{t}^{3}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C,$ we use the fact that $v(0)=0.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
0=\frac{1}{6}({0}^{3})+C\,⟹\,C=0.
$$

Hence, the velocity of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=\frac{1}{6}{t}^{3}.$ In particular, its inital velocity at time $t=1\,s$ and final velocity at time $t=2\,s$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{0} & =v(1)=\frac{1}{6}({1}^{3})=\frac{1}{6}\,m/s, \\ {v}_{1} & =v(2)=\frac{1}{6}({2}^{3})=\frac{4}{3}\,m/s.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the change in kinetic energy of the particle between these times is

$$
\begin{aligned}Δ\,\text{KE} & =\frac{1}{2}m{v}_{1}^{2}-\frac{1}{2}m{v}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 3\cdot {(\frac{4}{3})}^{2}-\frac{1}{2}\cdot 3\cdot {(\frac{1}{6})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{8}{3}-\frac{1}{24} \\  & =\frac{21}{8}\,J.\end{aligned}
$$
